findings.problem: Line 5 reads 'He will freely pardon (Isa 55:6-7). FREELY. Same price tag as the water!' This treats 'freely' in Isaiah 55:7 as 'free of charge' and ties the pardon to the water offered 'without money and without cost' in Isaiah 55:1. The BSB's 'freely' can be read as 'free of cost', but it can also mean 'generously' or 'abundantly', and the text never links the pardon in 55:7 to the price of the water in 55:1. The docs say to leave open how two things connect and that what he notices must be true, but they don't say whether a play on one English word's double meaning counts as connecting two things.
findings.question: Can Papa Dorin play on the BSB's 'freely pardon' (Isa 55:7) as 'free of cost' and link it to the 'without cost' water of Isaiah 55:1 ('Same price tag as the water!'), or should the line keep 'freely' without tying it to the price in 55:1?
